tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move to the list, check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the move respects size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you propose a move, verify that the source peg's top disk matches the disk you intend to move and that the destination peg can accept it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk from a peg where it is not the topmost disk or does not exist, such as moving disk 5 from peg 1 when it is actually on peg 0.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints; use it to temporarily free larger disks or to hold a place while larger moves are made.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by a smaller disk on its peg, move the smallest disk to another peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the smallest disk onto the target peg before moving the largest disk, which then blocks the larger disk from being placed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top of them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has correctly placed larger disks, avoid moving them and only add smaller disks above.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed large disk off the target peg, breaking the final order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg before moving to the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration, start with the largest disk and work downwards.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing smaller disks onto the target peg before the larger disks, causing the larger disks to be blocked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, ensure the last syntactically correct list in the response is the move list, so the verifier can parse it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of your answer, output the move list as a single JSON-like list without extra trailing text.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving the move list out of the final answer or adding extra commentary after it, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure source and destination pegs are clear of smaller disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, make sure its source peg has no smaller disks on top and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you move a disk that is not the smallest, check both source and destination pegs for smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg that already contains disk 1, violating the size ordering rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the answer short and within token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, aim for the minimal number of moves or a compact representation.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an excessively long move list that exceeds the allowed token budget.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, mentally simulate each move on the initial configuration to ensure the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing your answer, check that applying all moves results in the desired final state.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg, so the final configuration does not match the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks from auxiliary to destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a sub‑tower of multiple disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a stack of three disks directly without using the recursive pattern, leading to illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may think the answer is implicit or forget to include the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a complete move list as the final parseable list in the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may not check the size constraint when selecting the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving a disk, ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget that only the topmost disk can be moved from a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the disk you intend to move is the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generating before completing the sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Verify that the move list includes all necessary moves to reach the goal before submitting.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of disk locations during reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an updated representation of each peg's contents after each move.
